title: Gatekeeper adjudication for entitlement and org-policy requests
creator: Aisha Kumar
description:
Problem: Enterprise customers submit a broad set of non-bug admin requests (RBAC role templates, SSO/SAML configuration changes, SCIM schema updates, org policy exceptions). Current intake is inconsistent: requests land in support, sales, and PM inboxes with varying context, leading to long cycle times, missed compliance checks, and ad-hoc engineering work. Goal: design a deterministic "Gatekeeper" adjudication layer in the intake flow that automatically scores, classifies, and routes admin & access management requests to the right owners and queues while enforcing security gating for high-risk changes.

Scope: triage rules and scoring for RBAC/entitlement changes, SSO/SAML config requests, SCIM schema/connector changes, org policy exceptions (data retention, IP allowlists). Includes intake form changes, routing rules, automated notifications, and an audit log for decisions. Not in scope: building the RBAC engine itself or implementing SCIM connectors end-to-end (engineering tickets will be spawned).

Success criteria: reduced median time-to-first-action from support to owning team by 50% for enterprise admin requests; 100% of SAML/SCIM changes go through security review when flagged; clear owner assigned within 4 business hours for 95% of incoming requests.
acceptance_criteria: Public intake form with required structured fields deployed (customer tier, change type, number of effected users, description of business justification, security/regulatory notes)
Automated scoring engine assigns a triage score and routes to: Support Ops, Security Review, Identity Platform Eng, Product PM, or Solutions Eng based on deterministic rules
Routing rules and score thresholds documented in Confluence; routing test harness shows expected outcomes for 12 representative request templates
Audit log captures original request, score, routing decision, and approver actions for 180 days
Metrics dashboard shows median time-to-owner, time-in-queue by team, and percentage escalated to security
notes: We should reuse existing intake web UI used for Dedicated/Private onboarding to minimize frontend work (DES-214) and prefill org metadata where possible
Working assumption: enterprise tier and SSO metadata accessible via org profile to auto-populate form fields
Security will require metadata validation for SAML changes (thumbprint checks, metadata URL verification) before routing to engineering
Consider a temporary human-in-the-loop fallback (Support Ops) for first 30 days after launch to catch misclassifications

triage_rubric: Scoring components: customer_tier (0-30), affected_seats (0-20), security_risk (0-30), regulatory_impact (0-15), urgency (0-5)
Thresholds: 0-24 -> Support Ops; 25-54 -> PM/Solutions review; 55+ or security_risk >= 20 -> Security + ID Eng escalation
Automated flags: SAML metadata present -> force security_review=true; SCIM schema change -> compatibility flag required
Edge rules: requests from 'enterprise-SLA' customers escalate one priority level automatically; requests tagged 'data-region-change' require Legal review
routing_matrix_examples: Example A: RBAC role addition for 5 users, customer_tier=Standard (score 18) -> Support Ops route, Solutions Consult optional
Example B: SAML metadata update for enterprise-SLA customer, security_risk=25 -> Immediate Security Review + ID Eng, owner assigned within 1 business hour
Example C: SCIM schema change affecting attributes mapping (compatibility=false), affected_seats=200 -> Route to ID Eng + Solutions + PM, include migration plan request
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (2 weeks): service-side scoring + routing with human-in-the-loop (Support Ops). Phase 2 (4 weeks): automated routing to queues + audit log enabled. Phase 3 (8 weeks): add telemetry-driven reweighting and self-serve approvals for low-risk RBAC changes.
implementation_notes: Engineering needs a webhook endpoint to accept validated intake payloads (ENG-5023)
Design to provide updated intake UI components and microcopy (DES-214)
Support to own the human fallback runbook and SLA during rollouts
Legal to review templates for org-policy exceptions that touch data residency
